raw_response:
I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I farm for steady grain, manageable labor, and lower risk, so I will not spread myself across too many crops. In Quzhou County, this rotation fits the climate, the local water and machinery situation, and what I know how to manage well. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level instead of pushing too hard, because I want dependable yield more than high input cost. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, one topdressing, two irrigations if water allows, and a few pesticide sprays only when disease or insects show up. After wheat harvest, I will put in summer maize quickly, keep the field cleaner with simpler management, use improved or hybrid seed for stable stand and yield, and irrigate at the key stages instead of watering too often. I will use rotary tillage before wheat and no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and moisture.
